/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :

  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)

  rw [accCube_explicit, accCube_explicit]
  change ∑ i : Fin n, ((((fun a => a^3) ∘ S) (f.symm i))) = _
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Basic
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.GroupActions
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fintype
/-!
# Permutations of Pure U(1) ACC

We define the permutation group action on the charges of the Pure U(1) ACC system.
We further define the action on the ACC System.

-/

universe v u

open Nat
open Finset

namespace PureU1

/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from `Equiv.Perm`. -/
instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

open BigOperators
lemma accCube_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    accCube n (permCharges f S) = accCube n S := by
  rw [accCube_explicit, accCube_explicit]
  change ∑ i : Fin n, ((((fun a => a^3) ∘ S) (f.symm i))) = _
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

end Charges

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

lemma FamilyPermutations_charges_apply (S : (PureU1 n).Charges)
    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).rep f S) i = S (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

lemma FamilyPermutations_anomalyFreeLinear_apply (S : (PureU1 n).LinSols)
    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).linSolRep f S).val i = S.val (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

/-- The permutation which swaps i and j. -/
def pairSwap {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (FamilyPermutations n).group where
  toFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else
        s
  invFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else
        s
  left_inv s := by
    aesop
  right_inv s := by
    aesop

lemma pairSwap_self_inv {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j)⁻¹ = (pairSwap i j) := by
  rfl

lemma pairSwap_fst {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).toFun i = j := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_snd {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).toFun j = i := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_inv_fst {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).invFun i = j := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_inv_snd {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).invFun j = i := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_other {n : ℕ} (i j k : Fin n) (hik : i ≠ k) (hjk : j ≠ k) :
    (pairSwap i j).toFun k = k := by
  simp only [pairSwap, Equiv.toFun_as_coe, Equiv.coe_fn_mk]
  split
  · rename_i h
    exact False.elim (hik (id (Eq.symm h)))
  · split
    · rename_i h
      exact False.elim (hjk (id (Eq.symm h)))
    · rfl

lemma pairSwap_inv_other {n : ℕ} {i j k : Fin n} (hik : i ≠ k) (hjk : j ≠ k) :
    (pairSwap i j).invFun k = k := by
  simp only [pairSwap, Equiv.invFun_as_coe, Equiv.coe_fn_symm_mk]
  split
  · rename_i h
    exact False.elim (hik (id (Eq.symm h)))
  · split
    · rename_i h
      exact False.elim (hjk (id (Eq.symm h)))
    · rfl

/-- A permutation of fermions which takes one ordered subset into another. -/
noncomputable def permOfInjection (f g : Fin m ↪ Fin n) : (FamilyPermutations n).group :=
  Equiv.extendSubtype (g.toEquivRange.symm.trans f.toEquivRange)

variable {i j i' j' : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) (hij' : i' ≠ j')

def permTwoInj : Fin 2 ↪ Fin n where
  toFun s := match s with
    | 0 => i
    | 1 => j
  inj' s1 s2 := by
    aesop

lemma permTwoInj_fst_apply :
    (Function.Embedding.toEquivRange (permTwoInj hij)).symm ⟨i, permTwoInj_fst hij⟩ = 0 := by
  exact (Equiv.symm_apply_eq (Function.Embedding.toEquivRange (permTwoInj hij))).mpr rfl

lemma permTwoInj_snd : j ∈ Set.range ⇑(permTwoInj hij) := by
  simp only [Set.mem_range]

  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹

  map_one' := by rfl

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Basic
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.GroupActions
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fintype
/-!
# Permutations of Pure U(1) ACC

We define the permutation group action on the charges of the Pure U(1) ACC system.
We further define the action on the ACC System.

-/

universe v u

open Nat
open Finset

namespace PureU1

/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from `Equiv.Perm`. -/
instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

open BigOperators
lemma accCube_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    accCube n (permCharges f S) = accCube n S := by
  rw [accCube_explicit, accCube_explicit]
  change ∑ i : Fin n, ((((fun a => a^3) ∘ S) (f.symm i))) = _
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

end Charges

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).rep f S) i = S (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).linSolRep f S).val i = S.val (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Basic

/-!
# Permutations of Pure U(1) ACC

We define the permutation group action on the charges of the Pure U(1) ACC system.
We further define the action on the ACC System.

-/

universe v u

open Nat
open Finset

namespace PureU1

/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from `Equiv.Perm`. -/
instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

open BigOperators
lemma accCube_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    accCube n (permCharges f S) = accCube n S := by
  rw [accCube_explicit, accCube_explicit]
  change ∑ i : Fin n, ((((fun a => a^3) ∘ S) (f.symm i))) = _
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

end Charges

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

  rfl

    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).linSolRep f S).val i = S.val (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

/-!
# Permutations of Pure U(1) ACC

We define the permutation group action on the charges of the Pure U(1) ACC system.
We further define the action on the ACC System.

-/

universe v u

open Nat
open Finset

namespace PureU1

/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from `Equiv.Perm`. -/
instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

open BigOperators
lemma accCube_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    accCube n (permCharges f S) = accCube n S := by
  rw [accCube_explicit, accCube_explicit]
  change ∑ i : Fin n, ((((fun a => a^3) ∘ S) (f.symm i))) = _
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

end Charges

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

lemma FamilyPermutations_charges_apply (S : (PureU1 n).Charges)
    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).rep f S) i = S (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

lemma FamilyPermutations_anomalyFreeLinear_apply (S : (PureU1 n).LinSols)
    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).linSolRep f S).val i = S.val (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

/-- The permutation which swaps i and j. -/
def pairSwap {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (FamilyPermutations n).group where
  toFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else
        s
  invFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else
        s
  left_inv s := by
    aesop
  right_inv s := by
    aesop

lemma pairSwap_self_inv {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j)⁻¹ = (pairSwap i j) := by
  rfl

lemma pairSwap_fst {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).toFun i = j := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_snd {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).toFun j = i := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_inv_fst {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).invFun i = j := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_inv_snd {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).invFun j = i := by
  simp [pairSwap]

lemma pairSwap_other {n : ℕ} (i j k : Fin n) (hik : i ≠ k) (hjk : j ≠ k) :
    (pairSwap i j).toFun k = k := by
  simp only [pairSwap, Equiv.toFun_as_coe, Equiv.coe_fn_mk]

    exact False.elim (hik (id (Eq.symm h)))
  · split
    · rename_i h

    · rfl

    exact False.elim (hik (id (Eq.symm h)))
  · split
    · rename_i h
      exact False.elim (hjk (id (Eq.symm h)))
    · rfl

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Basic
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.GroupActions
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fintype
/-!
# Permutations of Pure U(1) ACC

We define the permutation group action on the charges of the Pure U(1) ACC system.
We further define the action on the ACC System.

-/

universe v u

open Nat
open Finset

namespace PureU1

/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from `Equiv.Perm`. -/
instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

open BigOperators
lemma accCube_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    accCube n (permCharges f S) = accCube n S := by
  rw [accCube_explicit, accCube_explicit]
  change ∑ i : Fin n, ((((fun a => a^3) ∘ S) (f.symm i))) = _
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

end Charges

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :

  rfl

    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).linSolRep f S).val i = S.val (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Basic
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.GroupActions
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fintype
/-!
# Permutations of Pure U(1) ACC

We define the permutation group action on the charges of the Pure U(1) ACC system.
We further define the action on the ACC System.

-/

universe v u

open Nat
open Finset

namespace PureU1

/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from `Equiv.Perm`. -/
instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

open BigOperators
lemma accCube_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    accCube n (permCharges f S) = accCube n S := by
  rw [accCube_explicit, accCube_explicit]
  change ∑ i : Fin n, ((((fun a => a^3) ∘ S) (f.symm i))) = _
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp

end Charges

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

lemma FamilyPermutations_charges_apply (S : (PureU1 n).Charges)
    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).rep f S) i = S (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

lemma FamilyPermutations_anomalyFreeLinear_apply (S : (PureU1 n).LinSols)
    (i : Fin n) (f : (FamilyPermutations n).group) :
    ((FamilyPermutations n).linSolRep f S).val i = S.val (f.invFun i) := by
  rfl

/-- The permutation which swaps i and j. -/
def pairSwap {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (FamilyPermutations n).group where
  toFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else
        s
  invFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else

  left_inv s := by
    aesop
  right_inv s := by
    aesop

lemma pairSwap_self_inv {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j)⁻¹ = (pairSwap i j) := by

lemma pairSwap_fst {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (pairSwap i j).toFun i = j := by

    (pairSwap i j).toFun k = k := by
  simp only [pairSwap, Equiv.toFun_as_coe, Equiv.coe_fn_mk]
  split
  · rename_i h
    exact False.elim (hik (id (Eq.symm h)))
  · split
    · rename_i h
      exact False.elim (hjk (id (Eq.symm h)))
    · rfl

    (pairSwap i j).invFun k = k := by
  /-
    n : Nat
    i j k : Fin n
    hik : Ne i k
    hjk : Ne j k
    ⊢ Eq ((PureU1.pairSwap i j).invFun k) k
  -/
  simp only [pairSwap, Equiv.invFun_as_coe, Equiv.coe_fn_symm_mk]
  /-
    n : Nat
    i j k : Fin n
    hik : Ne i k
    hjk : Ne j k
    ⊢ Eq (ite (Eq k i) j (ite (Eq k j) i k)) k
  -/
  split
    /-
      case isTrue
      n : Nat
      i j k : Fin n
      hik : Ne i k
      hjk : Ne j k
      h✝ : Eq k i
      ⊢ Eq j k
    -/
  · rename_i h
    /-
      case isTrue
      n : Nat
      i j k : Fin n
      hik : Ne i k
      hjk : Ne j k
      h : Eq k i
      ⊢ Eq j k
    -/
    exact False.elim (hik (id (Eq.symm h)))
    /-
      🎉 no goals
    -/
    /-
      case isFalse
      n : Nat
      i j k : Fin n
      hik : Ne i k
      hjk : Ne j k
      h✝ : Not (Eq k i)
      ⊢ Eq (ite (Eq k j) i k) k
    -/

      /-
        case isFalse.isTrue
        n : Nat
        i j k : Fin n
        hik : Ne i k
        hjk : Ne j k
        h✝¹ : Not (Eq k i)
        h✝ : Eq k j

      -/
    · rename_i h

        hik : Ne i k

        h✝ : Not (Eq k i)
        h : Eq k j
        ⊢ Eq i k
      -/
      exact False.elim (hjk (id (Eq.symm h)))
      /-
        🎉 no goals
      -/
      /-
        case isFalse.isFalse
        n : Nat
        i j k : Fin n
        hik : Ne i k
        hjk : Ne j k
        h✝¹ : Not (Eq k i)

Because this is in the `Eq` namespace, if you have a variable `h : a = b`,
`h.symm` can be used as shorthand for `Eq.symm h` as a proof of `b = a`.

Although this may look like a useless function, one application of the identity
function is to explicitly put a type on an expression. If `e` has type `T`,

knows that this expression has type `T'` rather than `T`. This can make a
difference for typeclass inference, since `T` and `T'` may have different
typeclass instances on them. `show T' from e` is sugar for an `@id T' e`
expression.
-/

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`False.elim : False → C` says that from `False`, any desired proposition
`C` holds. Also known as ex falso quodlibet (EFQ) or the principle of explosion.

The target type is actually `C : Sort u` which means it works for both
propositions and types. When executed, this acts like an "unreachable"
instruction: it is **undefined behavior** to run, but it will probably print
"unreachable code". (You would need to construct a proof of false to run it
anyway, which you can only do using `sorry` or unsound axioms.)
-/

  h.rec

informal_statement: A permutation of fermions rearranges the ordered subsets of fermions, reflecting their indistinguishability and anti-symmetry in quantum mechanics.
informal_proof:
To understand how permutations of fermions rearrange their ordered subsets, we start by considering the fundamental properties of fermions, which are particles with half-integer spin that obey the Pauli exclusion principle. This principle states that no two fermions can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously. As such, fermions are considered indistinguishable in terms of their individual identities.

When applying a permutation to a set of fermions, we are effectively rearranging their positions or roles within the system. For an ordered subset of fermions, this permutation can be seen as a transformation that maps one specific ordering of fermions to another. Since fermions are indistinct, such a permutation does not change their overall quantum state but alters their configuration in a way that must respect the principles of quantum mechanics.

The anti-symmetry property of fermions plays a crucial role in determining how these permutations affect the system's state. Specifically, swapping two fermions results in a sign change of the wavefunction, which ensures the overall anti-symmetry of the fermionic state. This property must be taken into account when considering the rearrangement of ordered subsets, as it dictates the allowable transformations and their implications for the system's quantum state.

By applying these principles, we recognize that a permutation of fermions rearranges the ordered subsets in a manner that preserves the anti-symmetric nature of their quantum state while respecting the Pauli exclusion principle. This ensures that the system's physical properties remain consistent and that the indistinguishability of fermions is preserved under such permutations.

We further define the action on the ACC System.

@[simp]

instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

@[simp]

  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹

  map_one' := by rfl

  /-
    n : Nat

  -/
  simp only [pairSwap, Equiv.toFun_as_coe, Equiv.coe_fn_mk]
  /-
    n : Nat
    i j k : Fin n
    hik : Ne i k
    hjk : Ne j k
    ⊢ Eq (ite (Eq k i) j (ite (Eq k j) i k)) k
  -/
  split
    /-
      case isTrue
      n : Nat
      i j k : Fin n
      hik : Ne i k
      hjk : Ne j k
      h✝ : Eq k i
      ⊢ Eq j k
    -/
  · rename_i h
    /-
      case isTrue
      n : Nat
      i j k : Fin n
      hik : Ne i k
      hjk : Ne j k
      h : Eq k i
      ⊢ Eq j k
    -/
    exact False.elim (hik (id (Eq.symm h)))

      🎉 no goals
    -/
    /-
      case isFalse
      n : Nat
      i j k : Fin n
      hik : Ne i k
      hjk : Ne j k
      h✝ : Not (Eq k i)

Because this is in the `Eq` namespace, if you have a variable `h : a = b`,

The identity function. `id` takes an implicit argument `α : Sort u`
(a type in any universe), and an argument `a : α`, and returns `a`.

Although this may look like a useless function, one application of the identity
function is to explicitly put a type on an expression. If `e` has type `T`,
and `T'` is definitionally equal to `T`, then `@id T' e` typechecks, and Lean
knows that this expression has type `T'` rather than `T`. This can make a
difference for typeclass inference, since `T` and `T'` may have different
typeclass instances on them. `show T' from e` is sugar for an `@id T' e`
expression.

/--
`False.elim : False → C` says that from `False`, any desired proposition
`C` holds. Also known as ex falso quodlibet (EFQ) or the principle of explosion.

The target type is actually `C : Sort u` which means it works for both
propositions and types. When executed, this acts like an "unreachable"
instruction: it is **undefined behavior** to run, but it will probably print
"unreachable code". (You would need to construct a proof of false to run it
anyway, which you can only do using `sorry` or unsound axioms.)
-/

  h.rec

open Nat Finset

universe v u
informal_statement: For any natural number \( n \) and distinct indices \( i, j, k \) in \( \text{Fin}(n) \), swapping \( i \) and \( j \) and then inverting the resulting permutation results in the original index \( k \).
informal_proof: Let \( n \) be a natural number and suppose \( i, j, k \) are distinct elements in \( \text{Fin}(n) \). When we swap \( i \) and \( j \), we create a permutation where \( i \) and \( j \) are interchanged. To invert this permutation, we effectively reverse the swap, returning all elements to their original positions. Specifically, since \( k \) was not involved in the swap, swapping \( i \) and \( j \) does not affect \( k \). Therefore, applying the inverse permutation after the swap cancels out the swap, leaving \( k \) unchanged. Thus, the composition of swapping \( i \) and \( j \) followed by inverting the permutation results in \( k \).

<PROOF>
To understand why swapping \( i \) and \( j \) does not affect \( k \), let's consider the process of swapping. Swapping \( i \) and \( j \) means exchanging their positions. However, since \( k \) is distinct from both \( i \) and \( j \), it is not involved in this exchange.

Mathematically, a swap operation on \( i \) and \( j \) can be represented as a function that maps \( i \) to \( j \), \( j \) to \( i \), and leaves all other elements unchanged. When this function is applied to \( k \), which is neither \( i \) nor \( j \), the result remains \( k \) since \( k \) isn't altered by the swap.

Therefore, for \( k \) ≠ \( i \) and \( k \) ≠ \( j \), the element \( k \) remains invariant under the swap of \( i \) and \( j \).

namespace PureU1

open Nat Finset

universe v u
informal_statement: For any two distinct indices `i` and `j` in the finite set `Fin n`, swapping `i` and `j` and then applying the inverse swap operation to `i` results in `j`.
informal_proof:
Consider the finite set `Fin n` and two distinct indices `i` and `j` within this set. The swap operation, denoted as `pairSwap i j`, creates a permutation where the elements at positions `i` and `j` are exchanged. Specifically, this permutation maps `i` to `j` and `j` to `i`. 

The inverse of a permutation, in general, "undoes" the permutation. Therefore, applying the inverse of the swap, `pairSwap i j`.invFun, to the permuted position `i` should result in the original position `j`. This is because the inverse operation reverses the effect of the permutation. 

To illustrate this, let's denote the swap permutation as σ. Then, σ(i) = j. The inverse permutation σ⁻¹ satisfies σ(σ⁻¹(i)) = i. Given that σ is simply the swap of `i` and `j`, the inverse permutation σ⁻¹ is equivalent to σ itself because swapping twice reverts the elements back to their original positions. Therefore, σ⁻¹(i) = σ(i) = j.

informal_statement: Swapping the `i`-th and `j`-th elements of a pair and then accessing the `i`-th element results in the original `j`-th element.
informal_proof: Consider a pair \((a, b)\) where \(a\) is the \(i\)-th element and \(b\) is the \(j\)-th element. When we apply the `pairSwap i j` operation, it swaps the positions of \(a\) and \(b\), resulting in \((b, a)\). Accessing the \(i\)-th element of this new pair yields \(b\), which was originally the \(j\)-th element of the original pair. Therefore, \((pairSwap\ i\ j).toFun\ i\) indeed equals \(j\).

informal_statement: For any two distinct elements \( i \) and \( j \) in \( \text{Fin}\ n \), the operation \( \text{pairSwap}(i, j) \) is its own inverse. This means that applying \( \text{pairSwap}(i, j) \) twice will restore the original configuration.
informal_proof:
First, we define the concept of an inverse operation. An operation \( f \) is considered an inverse of another operation \( g \) if applying \( f \) after \( g \) (or vice versa) returns the system to its original state. In other words, \( f(g(x)) = x \) and \( g(f(x)) = x \).

In the context of swapping two distinct elements \( i \) and \( j \) in \( \text{Fin}\ n \), the operation \( \text{pairSwap}(i, j) \) exchanges their positions. To be its own inverse, applying \( \text{pairSwap}(i, j) \) once should change \( i \) and \( j \), and applying it again should swap them back to their original positions.

Consider an example with a finite set \( \text{Fin}\ n \), where \( n \) represents the number of elements. Suppose we have a sequence of elements [..., \( a \), \( i \), \( j \), \( c \), ...]. Applying \( \text{pairSwap}(i, j) \) once changes the sequence to [..., \( a \), \( j \), \( i \), \( c \), ...]. Applying \( \text{pairSwap}(i, j) \) again swaps \( j \) and \( i \) back to their original positions, resulting in [..., \( a \), \( i \), \( j \), \( c \), ...]. This demonstrates that \( \text{pairSwap}(i, j) \) is indeed its own inverse because swapping twice reverts the sequence to the starting configuration.

informal_statement: For a given family of permutations and linear solutions, applying a permutation group element and evaluating it at a specific element 'i' yields the same result as evaluating the original solution at the inverse of that permutation applied to 'i'. This relationship holds true across the entire solution space and permutation group.
informal_proof:
To understand why this statement holds, consider that the permutation group element and its inverse act to reorder the elements in a way that preserves the structure of the solutions. When we apply the group element to the solution at point 'i', it effectively reorders the solution according to the permutation, which is equivalent to first reversing the permutation (using the inverse) and then evaluating at 'i'. This symmetry ensures that the solution's value remains consistent under these transformation operations.

Thus, the reflexivity inherent in the proof reflects that the group action preserves the solutions' properties when considering both the permutation and its inverse, maintaining the equality of the evaluated solutions across these transformations.

<PROOF>

To establish the invariance under permutations, we consider three cases: linear, quadratic, and cubic invariants.

**Linear Invariant:**
Given a linear combination of ACC system elements, permuting the system's components does not alter the linear relationships. This is because permutations merely rearrange the elements without affecting the coefficients or the underlying linear structure.

**Quadratic Invariant:**
For quadratic forms associated with the ACC system, the permutation acts on the variables. The quadratic form remains invariant under such permutations, as the symmetry of the quadratic form ensures that the rearrangement of variables does not change the outcome.

**Cubic Invariant:**
The cubic invariants involve three-way interactions among the system's components. Under permutation, these interactions are preserved since permutations can reorder elements without affecting their higher-order relationships.

Each invariant maintains its form under these transformations, confirming the existence of a consistent structure preserved by the permutations.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Basic

/-!
# Permutations of Pure U(1) ACC

We define the permutation group action on the charges of the Pure U(1) ACC system.
We further define the action on the ACC System.

-/

universe v u

open Nat
open Finset

namespace PureU1

/-- The permutation group of the n-fermions. -/
@[simp]
def PermGroup (n : ℕ) := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)

/-- The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from `Equiv.Perm`. -/
instance {n : ℕ} : Group (PermGroup n) := Equiv.Perm.permGroup

section Charges

/-- The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges. -/
@[simps!]
def chargeMap {n : ℕ} (f : PermGroup n) :
    (PureU1 n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun S := S ∘ f.toFun
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _:= rfl

/-- The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges. -/
@[simp]
def permCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (PureU1 n).Charges where
  toFun f := chargeMap f⁻¹
  map_mul' f g := by rfl
  map_one' := by rfl

lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  simp
annotation:
lemma accGrav_invariant {n : ℕ} (f : (PermGroup n)) (S : (PureU1 n).Charges) :
    PureU1.accGrav n (permCharges f S) = accGrav n S := by
  simp only [accGrav, PermGroup, permCharges, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk, chargeMap_apply]
  /-
    n : Nat
    f : PureU1.PermGroup n
    S : (PureU1 n).Charges
    ⊢ Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun x => S ((Inv.inv f) x)) (Finset.univ.sum fun i => S i)
  -/
  apply (Equiv.Perm.sum_comp _ _ _ ?_)
  /-
    n : Nat
    f : PureU1.PermGroup n
    S : (PureU1 n).Charges
    ⊢ HasSubset.Subset (setOf fun a => Ne ((Inv.inv f) a) a) ↑Finset.univ
  -/
  simp
  /-
    🎉 no goals
  -/

universe v u
informal_statement: Given a permutation \( f \) of the symmetric group on \( n \) elements and a charge configuration \( S \), the value \( \text{accCube}(n, S) \) remains unchanged under the permutation \( f \). This means that the invariant property of \( \text{accCube} \) is preserved regardless of how the elements are rearranged.
informal_proof:
To establish the invariance of \( \text{accCube}(n, S) \) under permutation \( f \), we consider the definition of \( \text{accCube} \) as a sum over the indices with respect to the permuted charges. Specifically, \( \text{accCube}(n, S) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} S(f(i)) \), where \( f(i) \) denotes the permutation applied to the \( i \)-th index.

The critical observation is that a permutation merely rearranges the order of the elements without altering their fundamental properties. Therefore, the sum \( \sum_{i=1}^{n} S(f(i)) \) essentially reflects the same charge configuration \( S \) but viewed under a different ordering of indices. 

Since the sum of a set of values is independent of the order in which they are summed, it follows that \( \sum_{i=1}^{n} S(f(i)) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} S(i) \). This equality demonstrates the invariance of \( \text{accCube}(n, S) \) under the permutation \( f \), confirming that \( \text{accCube}(n, S) = \text{accCube}(n, f(S)) \).

This invariance can be formally verified by applying the permutation to the charges and demonstrating that the transformed charges yield the same `accGrav` value as the original charges. The proof would typically involve showing that the permutation operation does not alter the essential properties that `accGrav` relies on, thereby preserving its result.

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/--

informal_statement: The permutation group of n-fermions is the group of all possible rearrangements of n distinct fermions. This group captures the symmetries inherent in their arrangement and plays a fundamental role in quantum mechanics, where it helps describe the behavior and allowable states of identical fermions.
informal_proof:
1. We define the permutation group of n-fermions, denoted as \( S_n \), as the set of all possible bijections (one-to-one and onto functions) from the set of n-fermions to itself.
2. The group operation is defined as the composition of permutations, which is the application of one permutation after another.
3. The identity element is the identity permutation, which maps each fermion to itself.
4. For each permutation \( \sigma \) in \( S_n \), there exists an inverse permutation \( \sigma^{-1} \) such that the composition \( \sigma \circ \sigma^{-1} \) results in the identity permutation.
5. The composition of permutations is associative, meaning \( (\sigma \circ \tau) \circ \rho = \sigma \circ (\tau \circ \rho) \) for any permutations \( \sigma, \tau, \rho \) in \( S_n \).
6. Therefore, \( S_n \) satisfies all the group axioms: closure, associativity, identity, and inverses.
7. Specifically, \( S_n \) is isomorphic to the symmetric group on a set of n elements, well-known in mathematics and physics under the standard terminology.

This permutation group \( S_n \) is essential in quantum mechanics, particularly in describing the symmetry properties of identical fermions, which follow the Pauli exclusion principle. The group structure underpins the classification of fermionic states and their transformations under various physical operations.
